about: Every remote tool the app knows. `built: false` is a tool that is planned and refused; `gated: true` is a tool the remoteTools switch, the approved folders and the caps control. A tool not listed here is refused (unknown_tool). `gateway` is the name a tool has through the ChatGPT gateway (the gateway, docs/chatgpt-gateway.md); a row without it is not offered there. Read by the gateway crate at build time (core/src/remote/manifest.rs); see docs/settings.md.

tools.grant: CLI: Chat switch. Through the gateway (the engine path, `gated`): remoteGateway and remoteTools
tools.note: The CLI lists every chat from its own code, not this row. The gateway lists every chat that can be messaged (this computer and linked ones) with the value chat_send takes; only chats in remoteChatRead on this computer are marked readable and carry the value chat_read takes. Names and folders are redacted. A call from any other door keeps the old answer (the selected chats only).

tools.grant: CLI: Chat switch. Through the gateway: remoteGateway and remoteTools, and the Chat switch on this computer (no new switch)
tools.note: Through the gateway only, from the chat `chatgpt` (ChatGPT), never as another chat. Every message starts with a fixed line saying it is from ChatGPT, relayed by the gateway, unverified and not the user's words, and the sender name says the same. Text up to 32 KiB. A send cannot be taken back (destructiveHint true); to a chat on a linked computer it leaves this computer (openWorldHint true).

tools.grant: CLI: Chat switch. Through the gateway: remoteGateway and remoteTools, and the Chat switch on this computer (no new switch)
tools.note: Through the gateway only: answers a message ChatGPT's own chat received (the stored route must name `chatgpt` as the receiver), never as another chat, with the same unverified stamp. A message from a plain terminal takes no reply.

tools.grant: CLI: Chat switch. Through the gateway: remoteGateway and remoteTools; reads ChatGPT's own inbox only
tools.note: Through the gateway it reads only the messages sent to the ChatGPT chat (`<cli> chat send ChatGPT`), oldest first, redacted, bodies cut at 16 KiB, and changes nothing (afterSeq skips what was seen). ChatGPT is listed as a chat only while the gateway runs with both switches on. The CLI's inbox still returns the unread messages of every chat here and is not offered.

tools.grant: Chat switch
tools.note: Not offered through the gateway: it returns what the user typed in another chat's transcript, outside the remoteChatRead selection. chat_read is the gateway's transcript tool.

tools.grant: remoteTools, and the chat is in remoteChatRead
remoteTools, approved folder (remoteRoots)
tools.note: Kind, size, modification time. `tail` (1 to 1000 lines, from the last 256 KiB of a text file) and `sha256` (a file up to 1 GiB) are optional; through the gateway a secret-named file gets neither and tail text is redacted.

tools.grant: remoteTools, approved folder (remoteRoots)
remoteTools, approved folder (remoteRoots)
tools.note: By name, or with mode content by text inside files: approved folders only, text files up to 2 MiB (UTF-8, not secret-named), at most 256 MiB read, 8 seconds, 200000 entries; up to 3 matching lines per file, redacted through the gateway.

tools.grant: remoteTools, approved folder (remoteRoots)
tools.note: Returns one PNG, JPEG or GIF inside an approved folder exactly as it is on disk (base64, with mime, width and height from its header; the type comes from the bytes). There is no image decoder, so nothing is re-encoded or shrunk: a file over the smaller of remoteImageMaxBytes and 5 MiB is too_large, and so is an image whose longest side is above maxPixel. Any other format, SVG included, is unsupported_format. Secret-named files are refused through the gateway.

tools.grant: remoteGateway, remoteTools and remoteFilesWrite (off by default), approved folder (remoteRoots), one local approval per save, asked before any download
tools.note: Save ChatGPT's file (Zenon's download_artifact): the `file` object is ChatGPT's (openai/fileParams); the download URL must be https on a pinned OpenAI file host (exact names, re-observe on current builds), redirects are re-validated by hand, at most 32 MiB; written as a new file (exclusive create, never replaces) in an approved folder, hashed in a temporary file and read back; the answer has path, size and sha256. Gateway only. It is not a fetch-any-URL tool.

tools.grant: remoteTools (needs the task journal)
remoteTools (needs the task journal)
its own switch (context layer)
its own switch (context layer)
remoteTools and remoteFilesWrite (off by default), approved folder (remoteRoots), one local approval per act
tools.note: Edits one UTF-8 file by exact text (old must occur once) or creates a new file; temp-file hash and read-back verified; secret-named files refused. `files` takes up to 16 such changes in one call under one approval: all are checked before any is written, each is then written atomically and verified, and a failure part-way names how many were already changed.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteFilesWrite (off by default), approved folder (remoteRoots), one local approval per act
tools.note: mkdir, move, copy (never over an existing name) and trash. Trash is the macOS Trash or the Windows Recycle Bin (the answer has no trashedAs on Windows); other systems answer unsupported_platform. Nothing is deleted outright.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteDocs, approved folder (remoteRoots)
tools.note: Text of a PDF (or DOCX, XLSX) by page, bounded in size, pages and characters; secret-named files refused; through the gateway the text passes the secret redactor (redactions counts them). Writing is docs.write.

tools.grant: remoteGateway, remoteTools, remoteDocs and remoteFilesWrite (both off by default), approved folder (remoteRoots), one local approval per call
tools.note: Creates a new DOCX or XLSX (never over an existing name) or edits a DOCX, XLSX or PDF in place by rightkit-docs typed operations (replaceText, appendBlocks, setCells, appendRows, addPdfText, selectPdfPages); the approval binds the file's hash and the exact operations; refused while remoteReadOnly is on; read back and hash verified. No new PDF, no macros, no encrypted files.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteScreenObserve (off by default), the disclosure grant (remoteScreenDisclosure), OS permission; apps on remoteBlockedApps and the app, System Settings and security prompts are never shown
tools.note: Lists the on-screen windows of apps that are not blocked, or returns one window's accessibility tree and, on request, a redacted PNG. Secure and credential fields are withheld. The OS permission is checked, never requested (permission_missing).

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteTerminals (off by default), a local session approval per door or the remoteTermStanding policy; 30-minute idle expiry
tools.note: Runs exactly the command text it is given through /bin/sh -c (cmd.exe on Windows) on this computer as the user with a scrubbed environment; unrestricted user-level execution once approved, and the user's own deny and allow lists (remoteTermDeny, remoteTermAllow) are applied first. `cmds` runs up to 20 commands in turn; `tty: true` runs it on a pseudo-terminal. Refused while remoteReadOnly is on.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteTerminals (off by default), a local session approval per door or the remoteTermStanding policy; 30-minute idle expiry
remoteTools and remoteTerminals (off by default), a local session approval per door or the remoteTermStanding policy; 30-minute idle expiry
remoteTools and remoteTerminals (off by default), a local session approval per door or the remoteTermStanding policy; 30-minute idle expiry
remoteTools and remoteTerminals (off by default), a local session approval per door or the remoteTermStanding policy
tools.note: Lists this door's terminal sessions: id, pid, whether it is a pseudo-terminal and its size, whether it runs, waitingForInput (running, quiet, last line looks like a prompt), idle seconds and output bytes. Never the command or the output.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteTerminals (off by default), a local session approval per door or the remoteTermStanding policy; refused while remoteReadOnly is on
tools.note: Changes the rows (5 to 200) and columns (20 to 500) of a tty session started by term_exec.

tools.grant: remoteGateway, remoteTools and remoteTerminals, the terminal session grant, and the chat on the approved-chats list (remoteChatRead)
tools.note: Reads the recent screen text of a chat's live terminal. Only a chat running inside a tmux pane can be addressed (the chat's process or an ancestor is the pane's process); any other chat, a Codex thread, and Windows are refused not_addressable. Redacted, newest 64 KiB. Gateway only.

tools.grant: as chat_term_read, plus one local approval per write bound to the pane and the exact text; refused while remoteReadOnly is on
tools.note: Types up to 1000 characters (no control characters) into a chat's tmux pane, optionally followed by Return. Card numbers, bank details and IDs are refused. Gateway only.

tools.grant: remoteGateway, remoteTools, remoteClipboard (off by default) and the screen disclosure grant (remoteScreenDisclosure), one local approval per read bound to a hash of the current text
tools.note: Read only; there is no clipboard write. The approval shows the character count, never the text. Card numbers, bank details and IDs are refused; keys and tokens are masked; at most 64 KiB. macOS and Windows. Gateway only.

tools.grant: remoteGateway and remoteTools; only a chat this gateway process started with chat_start; no approval (it only ends work an approved start began)
tools.note: Ends the chat chat_start started (its descendants, then the program, each checked against the identity recorded at the start). Gateway only.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteTerminals (off by default), a local session approval per door or the remoteTermStanding policy; 30-minute idle expiry
tools.note: Only this user's processes; pid plus startTime identify one.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteTerminals (off by default), a local session approval per door or the remoteTermStanding policy; 30-minute idle expiry
tools.note: Verifies pid and start time twice and through RightKit's AdoptedIdentity before signalling; never the app or its parent.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteScreenAct (off by default), the disclosure grant, OS permission, no blocked app; the gateway needs one local approval per action bound to the target and the action, the local agent and the owner only for submit, buy, send, publish and delete controls
tools.note: Acts on a screen.observe snapshot: press, set_value, type_text, keys, click, scroll, focus, menu_press, handover (spot takeover #355, needs remoteScreenSpotTakeover on, off by default: the owner approves, bound to that window and element, and the takeover ends as target_moved when the window moves, resizes, retitles or closes; then only that element's region is shown on screen with the rest dimmed until the user presses Done or Cancel; every screen tool answers user_in_control meanwhile). A changed target is target_changed; never foreground input. Through the gateway every action is asked, except typing the user's own profile details (remoteFormFillProfile) into an app with a form-fill standing grant (remoteFormFill on); the local agent and the owner are not asked for ordinary actions. Passwords, card numbers, bank details and government IDs are never typed (sensitive_input); a submit, buy, send or publish control always asks.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteLaunch (off by default), the app is not on remoteBlockedApps (empty by default); local door: no approval; gateway: one local approval per app, then a standing grant (30 days without use)
tools.note: Opens any app that is not blocked, by bundle id (macOS, `open -b`) or AppUserModelID or full exe path (Windows). No arguments, URL or file. Served by the engine and offered to the always-on acting agent.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteMedia (off by default); no per-call approval
tools.note: play, pause, next, previous, search_play and now_playing (state, title, artist, album) for Spotify and Music; a blocked app or floor app is refused with app_blocked. macOS: Apple Events through osascript with a fixed script per verb, the query passed as an argument. Windows: the system media session (SMTC). Spotify search_play opens Spotify's search page; Music plays the first matching library track. Served by the engine and offered to the always-on acting agent.

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteFormFillLogins (off by default), an unlocked chat, a saved login for the page's host, one local approval per chat, host and login (Touch ID, Windows Hello or the PIN); local door only
tools.note: Types one field (username, password or totp) of a login saved in the app's secure box into the focused field of the browser in front, after the app reads the page's own address (Safari, Chrome, Brave, Edge on a Mac; https, default port) and finds it equal to the saved host; or starts a password manager the user listed (remoteFormFillLoginManagers) by its own autofill chord. The answer is filled or a refusal and never a value. On Windows the address comes from the address bar of Chrome, Edge, Brave or Firefox through UI Automation (a Chromium browser must show full URLs; otherwise origin_unreadable). Field totp types the current one-time code of a login saved with a TOTP secret, after the same page check and approval. Not offered through the gateway. Unproven: no run against a real browser (bogusyogi/pulse#345).

tools.grant: remoteTools and remoteFormFillPayments (off by default), an unlocked chat, a saved virtual card for the page's host; no question at or below the card's auto-approve limit, otherwise one local approval per purchase (Touch ID, Windows Hello or the PIN); local door only
tools.note: Types one field (number, expMonth, expYear, exp, cvv, name, zip) of a purchase into the focused field of the verified checkout page: `fields` names every card field the checkout needs (the same list on each call); one approval or automatic pass covers that chat, exact page address, card, amount and field set once, each field typed once; the amount is reserved against the month before typing, booked only after every field is typed, released if nothing was typed, otherwise recorded as unknown and still counted. Only a saved virtual or tokenized US card is used, inside the card's per-purchase and monthly limits and the owner's global caps (remoteFormFillPaymentsAutoCapCents default 2500 clamps every card's auto-approve limit; remoteFormFillPaymentsMonthCapCents default 10000 bounds the month over all cards), which the app applies to the agent's claimed amount; above the auto limit every purchase asks (Touch ID signature on a Mac, the PIN on Windows; Windows Hello is refused until it signs); a live purchase re-checks its reservation; US dollars only. The amount and the shop's name are the agent's claim and are shown to the owner as such. The answer is filled or a refusal and never a value. Pressing the pay button stays screen.act's own question. Not offered through the gateway. Unproven: no run against a real browser or a real card (bogusyogi/pulse#346).

tools.grant: remoteGateway and remoteTools, an approved folder (remoteRoots) as the working folder, one local approval per start bound to the kind, folder and exact prompt
tools.note: Starts a new Codex (`codex exec`) or Claude (`claude -p`) chat in an approved folder with a prompt that begins with the unverified-ChatGPT stamp and how to report back (`<cli> chat send ChatGPT`). Runs under that program's own default permissions (the app passes no flag that widens them), with a scrubbed environment, detached, its log a private file the app's tools never read. Gateway only.
